meta.title: Common Red Seal Welder Exam Traps
meta.description: Frequent trick patterns on the interprovincial welder exam. Each trap has a wrong assumption, the correct rule, and a memory hook.
sources: Red Seal Occupational Standard for Welder (2023)
Instructor feedback compiled from AIT/NAIT/SAIT program reviews

traps.when: Any question about E7018 or other low-hydrogen SMAW electrode setup
traps.correct_rule: E7018 runs on AC or DCEP (electrode positive) ONLY. Never DCEN.
traps.memory_hook: The '8' in E7018 → 8 is even → electrode POSITIVE (AC or DC+). If an answer says DCEN with E7018, it's wrong.

traps.wrong_assumption: E6010 can run on AC or DCEN
traps.correct_rule: E6010 runs on DCEP ONLY. Not AC, not DCEN.
traps.memory_hook: E6010 = deep penetration = electrons hitting the work = DCEP.

traps.wrong_assumption: GTAW aluminum uses DCEN like stainless
traps.correct_rule: GTAW aluminum uses AC. The AC positive half-cycle provides cathodic cleaning that breaks up the aluminum oxide layer.
traps.memory_hook: Aluminum oxide melts hotter than aluminum — needs AC cleaning action to be weldable.

traps.correct_rule: GMAW uses DCEP for standard steel welding. FCAW self-shielded (T-4, T-6, T-8) uses DCEN. Gas-shielded FCAW (T-1) uses DCEP.
traps.memory_hook: Wire process default = DCEP. Only self-shielded FCAW breaks the rule.

traps.correct_rule: 1G flat groove · 2G horizontal groove · 3G VERTICAL groove · 4G overhead groove. Fillets use F: 1F flat, 2F horizontal, 3F vertical, 4F overhead.
traps.memory_hook: Count up like climbing a wall: 1 flat, 2 horizontal, 3 vertical (climbing), 4 overhead (above your head).

traps.correct_rule: Pipe: 1G ROTATED (roll while welding, always flat), 2G FIXED vertical axis (horizontal weld), 5G FIXED horizontal axis (weld around, through flat/vertical/overhead), 6G FIXED 45° inclined (all positions plus transitions). 6G qualifies the widest range of production work.
traps.memory_hook: 6G = 6 = the number of position transitions welder must handle = most versatile qualification.

traps.wrong_assumption: The first digit is the amperage
traps.correct_rule: AWS A5.1: First TWO digits (or three for E1XX) = minimum tensile strength in KSI × 1000. E7018 = 70,000 psi. Third digit = position (1 = all). Last two digits together = coating and current type.
traps.memory_hook: E70XX = 70 ksi tensile. The 70 is the strength, not the amperage.

traps.correct_rule: H = diffusible hydrogen limit in mL per 100 g of deposited weld metal. H4 = 4 mL max (strictest). H8 = 8. H16 = 16 (loosest). R = moisture-resistant coating.
traps.memory_hook: Lower H number = LESS hydrogen = MORE crack-resistant. H4 is strictest.

traps.when: SMAW low-hydrogen storage or hydrogen cracking questions
traps.wrong_assumption: E7018 storage at room temperature is fine
traps.correct_rule: Once opened, E7018 must go into a rod oven at ~120°C (250°F). Moisture in the flux becomes hydrogen in the arc, which causes delayed cracking hours to days after welding.
traps.memory_hook: Low-hydrogen = keep it DRY. Hot rod oven, always.

traps.correct_rule: Three flames: NEUTRAL (equal O2/fuel, ONE bright cone, standard for cutting and welding), CARBURIZING/reducing (fuel-rich, feather at tip, for brazing/hardening), OXIDIZING (O2-rich, sharp short hissing cone, only for brass or fast OFC). Standard OFC preheat = neutral.
traps.memory_hook: One clean cone = neutral. Feather = fuel-rich. Sharp hiss = O2-rich.

traps.correct_rule: OFC only cuts CARBON STEEL and low-alloy steel. Does NOT cut stainless (chromium oxide blocks the reaction), aluminum (oxide melts hotter than metal), copper (thermal conductivity too high), or cast iron (graphite disrupts oxidation). Stainless/aluminum → use PAC (plasma).
traps.memory_hook: OFC = OXidation of iron. If the metal doesn't oxidize better than it melts, OFC can't cut it.

traps.correct_rule: Aluminum requires 100% argon (helium may be added for thicker sections). CO2 reacts with aluminum and creates defects. Never use CO2-containing gas on aluminum.
traps.memory_hook: Aluminum = pure Ar. CO2 poisons aluminum welds.

traps.correct_rule: Open-root stainless requires an argon (or N2) back-purge on the ID. Without it, the hot root oxidizes → straw/gold/blue/purple/black heat tint. Sugaring (heavy black scale) is always rejectable.
traps.memory_hook: Purple = last chance. Black = failed inspection.

traps.correct_rule: HI (kJ/mm) = (V × A × 60) ÷ (mm/min × 1000). The ×60 converts seconds to minutes. Common mistake: dropping the ×60 gives an answer 60× too small.
traps.memory_hook: V × A gives WATTS. To get kJ/mm you need the ×60 (min to sec) and ÷1000 (J to kJ).

traps.wrong_assumption: Sling load per leg = total load ÷ number of legs
traps.correct_rule: Load per leg = (Total ÷ Legs) ÷ cos(θ/2), where θ is the INCLUDED angle between legs. At 60° included angle, each leg is ~15% higher than the simple division. At 120° each leg carries the full load.
traps.memory_hook: More angle = more load. Never exceed 120° included angle per ASME B30.9.

traps.wrong_assumption: Fillet strength is calculated on the leg
traps.correct_rule: Fillet weld strength = throat × length × filler shear strength. For 90° equal-leg fillet, throat = leg × 0.707. Doubling the leg does NOT double strength — it doubles throat too but also doubles heat and cost.
traps.memory_hook: Leg is what you SEE. Throat is what WORKS. Multiply by 0.707 for 90° fillet.

traps.correct_rule: AWS A2.4: symbol BELOW the reference line = ARROW side. Symbol ABOVE the line = OTHER side. Symbols on both sides = weld both sides. This one has bitten every welder at least once.
traps.memory_hook: Below = Below the arrow = Arrow side (both start with 'A'). Above = Away from arrow = Other side.

traps.wrong_assumption: The circle and the flag mean the same thing
traps.correct_rule: Circle at the elbow = WELD ALL AROUND (perimeter of the joint). FLAG at the elbow = FIELD WELD (to be made on site, not in shop).
traps.memory_hook: Circle = round the joint (all around). Flag = flag on the site (field).

traps.correct_rule: Purchase = Deposit ÷ Efficiency. If you deposit 25 kg and efficiency is 60% (SMAW), you need 25 ÷ 0.60 = 41.7 kg of electrodes. Multiplying gives an answer that's less than the deposit — clearly wrong.
traps.memory_hook: If you throw away half your consumable, you need TWICE the deposit weight. Always DIVIDE, never multiply.

traps.correct_rule: Labour hours = arc-on hours ÷ operator factor. SMAW operator factor is typically 20-30% (lots of stub changes, chipping, positioning). So 8 hours of arc-on time is really ~30 hours of shift time.
traps.memory_hook: Divide by operator factor because you can't arc 100% of the shift.

traps.wrong_assumption: Preheat is optional if the metal is thick
traps.correct_rule: Preheat is REQUIRED as thickness and carbon-equivalent increase. CSA W59 Annex E and AWS D1.1 Annex I give the minimums by material group and thickness. Skipping preheat on thick carbon steel with low-hydrogen electrodes still risks cracking.
traps.memory_hook: Thicker + higher CE = more preheat. Never assume; check the table.

traps.correct_rule: MAX interpass temperature matters too. Q&T steels (A514/A517) lose strength if held above ~590°C. Austenitic stainless keeps interpass ≤175°C to avoid sensitization. Check the WPS both directions.
traps.memory_hook: Preheat is a floor; interpass is a ceiling. Both violate the WPS.

traps.correct_rule: Grind LONGITUDINAL (parallel to tungsten axis). Perpendicular grind marks focus current at the tip, causing arc instability. Also: pointed 2× diameter for DC, balled/truncated for AC.
traps.memory_hook: Long strokes along the tungsten, like grinding a pencil.

traps.correct_rule: Tungsten inclusions are REJECTABLE per AWS D1.6 and most codes. Caused by tungsten touching the puddle or filler rod. Fix: regrind, use dip-and-lift filler technique, maintain arc gap ~1× electrode diameter.
traps.memory_hook: Never touch. Even 1 touch = a defect and 5 minutes of rework.

traps.correct_rule: Crater cracks come from breaking the arc abruptly at the end of a weld. Molten metal solidifies from all sides toward the crater, concentrating shrinkage stress. Fix: taper down current (crater-fill), or restart the arc briefly to fill the crater.
traps.memory_hook: Don't drop the arc. Ease off the trigger like a car brake.

traps.when: Cracking questions on thick carbon steel
traps.correct_rule: Hydrogen-induced (cold) cracking appears HOURS TO DAYS after welding. Signature: longitudinal cracks on thicker carbon steel with low-hydrogen electrodes, most often in the HAZ. Prevention: dry E7018, correct preheat, low H4 electrodes.
traps.memory_hook: Delayed crack = hydrogen. Immediate crack = usually solidification/hot cracking.

traps.correct_rule: CAC-A leaves carbon deposits and a carburized layer on the gouged surface. AWS D1.1 clause 5.15 and CSA W59 require GRINDING to bright metal before welding. Skipping this causes porosity, hard HAZ, and hydrogen cracking.
traps.memory_hook: Gouge → grind → weld. Never gouge → weld.

traps.wrong_assumption: Arc blow is caused by wind
traps.correct_rule: Arc blow is MAGNETIC arc deflection, most common with DC and near edges/corners/work-lead attachment. Fixes: switch to AC (self-cancelling fields), demagnetize, split the work lead, wrap the lead, shorten the arc.
traps.memory_hook: SMAW arc blow = magnetic, not atmospheric. AC solves it because the field alternates.

traps.correct_rule: GMAW porosity is almost always a shielding-gas failure. Check FIRST: flow AT THE TORCH (not just regulator), draft/wind, cracked hose, spatter-blocked nozzle. Only after gas checks pass do you look at wire, base metal, or parameters.
traps.memory_hook: Porosity = gas problem until proven otherwise.

traps.wrong_assumption: CTWD and nozzle-to-work are the same
traps.correct_rule: CTWD = Contact-Tip-to-Work Distance, measured from the tip inside the nozzle. Nozzle-to-work is a different, shorter distance visible outside the nozzle. Longer CTWD = lower current (I²R heating in the extended wire).
traps.memory_hook: CTWD is HIDDEN. Nozzle-to-work is VISIBLE. Don't confuse them in troubleshooting.

traps.wrong_assumption: Any gas can achieve spray transfer
traps.correct_rule: Spray transfer needs ≥80% argon shielding AND current above the transition threshold. Pure CO2 forces globular transfer regardless of parameters. Spray is also restricted to flat/horizontal positions.
traps.memory_hook: Spray = Ar-rich gas + high current + flat/horizontal. Miss any one and you don't get spray.

traps.wrong_assumption: SAW can be done in any position
traps.correct_rule: SAW is limited to FLAT and near-flat positions (1G, 1F, 2F) because the granular flux must sit on the joint by gravity. True out-of-position SAW doesn't exist. Pipe SAW uses rotating positioners.
traps.memory_hook: Flux is a POWDER. Powder doesn't stick to vertical walls or ceilings.

traps.correct_rule: For a regular hex: C = F / cos(30°) = F × 1.155. C is always LARGER than F. Drawings can spec either — confirm which convention before cutting stock.
traps.memory_hook: Corner is Cornered farther out. C > F, by ~15%.

traps.wrong_assumption: Mitre angle = total elbow angle ÷ pieces
traps.correct_rule: Mitre angle per CUT = total ÷ (2 × pieces). A 2-piece 90° elbow has ONE cut at 45° (not 90° / 2 = 45° coincidentally, but derived from the doubling). A 3-piece 90° elbow has cuts at 22.5°, not 30°.
traps.memory_hook: Each cut is shared between two adjacent pieces — hence the 2× in the denominator.

traps.wrong_assumption: Stronger filler is always OK to substitute
traps.correct_rule: Filler metal classification is an ESSENTIAL VARIABLE in most codes. Even substituting a 'stronger' or 'better' filler can invalidate the WPS qualification. Always check with the welding supervisor or engineer; may require re-qualification.
traps.memory_hook: 'Better' is not the same as 'qualified'. Never substitute without approval.
